close_reason: Added TypeDiscriminator trait with const TYPE_TAG: &'static str and default validate_at_type() -> Result<(), TypeTagMismatch> method. Implemented for all 12 structs (NDay, RecurrenceRule, Location, VirtualLocation, Link, Relation, Participant, OffsetTrigger, AbsoluteTrigger, Alert, TimeZoneRule, TimeZone). Deserialize remains permissive for round-trip preservation per RFC 8984 §4.5.2 preserve-mandate (and per the AlertTrigger Unknown pattern); strict validation is opt-in via validate_at_type(). Added test validate_at_type_rejects_wrong_discriminator covering hostile inputs on NDay, Location, Alert. cargo test + clippy clean. Chose trait + per-struct impl over (a) custom Deserialize that errors on mismatch — would break forward-compat with future polymorphic sub-types, and (b) wide-stringification newtype — too invasive for the value delivered.
description:
**Contract risk**: every struct in the crate has

    #[serde(rename = \"@type\")]
    pub at_type: String,

with a docstring of the form \"Object type discriminator; always
\\\"NDay\\\" on the wire.\" But:

    let n: NDay = serde_json::from_value(json!({
        \"@type\": \"NotAnNDay\",
        \"day\": \"mo\"
    })).unwrap();
    assert_eq!(n.at_type, \"NotAnNDay\");  // passes — discriminator was NOT validated

The `Deserialize` derived for `NDay` (and every sibling) accepts any
string in `@type` and stores it in `at_type` verbatim. Symmetric on
the serialize side — whatever is in `at_type` ships, regardless of
the Rust type it's attached to.

**What goes wrong for callers**:
- A consumer that pattern-matches on `at_type` (\"is this really
  an NDay, or has the server confused itself?\") will be misled.
  The docstring promises \"always NDay\" but the type doesn't enforce.
- A consumer constructing one of these types via deserialize-of-an-
  arbitrary-JSON path (e.g. forwarding a wire blob from an upstream
  server) can produce a struct whose `at_type` mismatches its type,
  then ship that back out — propagating wire-invalid data.
- Refactoring to a server-side dispatcher that uses `at_type` to
  decide what to do is unsafe without an external validation step.

**Fix shape** (breaking change):
Option A: replace the per-struct `at_type: String` with a serde tag:
`#[serde(tag = \"@type\")]` on an outer wrapper enum that dispatches
to the correct variant. This is what serde would normally do, but
the crate has deliberately not used it (see PLAN.md §\"@type
discriminator\" — bare `String` was chosen for forward-compat with
unknown sub-object types). Breaking.
Option B: add a custom `Deserialize` for each struct that validates
`at_type == \"<TypeName>\"` and returns an error otherwise.
Breaking only for callers depending on the current permissive
deserialize.
Option C (most conservative): leave the type as-is, but amend the
per-field docstring from \"always X on the wire\" to \"set to X by
servers; this type does not validate the value on deserialize —
treat the field as untrusted if the source is not authenticated.\"
That's at least an honest contract.

The existing JMAP-mno4.7 bead defends the bare-String shape against
\"consistency\" PRs (correct — it diverges intentionally from
jscontact's `Option<String>` per RFC). That bead does NOT address
this distinct gap: even given the bare String, the type should
either enforce the value or stop promising it.
title: at_type: String fields do not enforce that the discriminator matches the struct type on deserialize — caller assumption that nday.at_type == "NDay" is wrong on hostile input
